root_cause.text: __ip6_tnl_rcv() in the IPv6 tunnel receive path validated/pulled the inner IP header with pskb_inet_may_pull() but did not handle VLAN-encapsulated sk_buffs, so later ECN decapsulation read an improperly prepared inner header and used uninitialized data.
root_cause.evidence: The fix replaces `if (!pskb_inet_may_pull(skb))` with `if (skb_vlan_inet_prepare(skb, true))`, and the commit message explicitly says the blamed commit “did not take care of VLAN encapsulations,” while KMSAN reports an uninitialized read in `IP6_ECN_decapsulate` reached from `__ip6_tnl_rcv()`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Use VLAN-aware skb preparation in the IPv6 tunnel receive path so VLAN-tagged packets are validated correctly and invalid ones are dropped.
intent_record.what: The receive-path condition was changed from negating pskb_inet_may_pull(skb) to directly checking skb_vlan_inet_prepare(skb, true) after skb_reset_network_header(skb), while keeping the same error accounting and drop path.
intent_record.how: At runtime, packet validation/preparation in the IPv6 tunnel receive path now uses VLAN-aware IP header preparation instead of a simpler pullability check, causing packets that fail VLAN/IP preparation to be counted as receive length/errors and dropped, and allowing properly VLAN-encapsulated packets to be handled correctly.

grouping_result.intent: Use VLAN-aware skb preparation in the IPv6 tunnel receive path so VLAN-tagged packets are validated correctly and invalid ones are dropped.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly addresses the root cause: __ip6_tnl_rcv() previously used non-VLAN-aware skb preparation, which mishandled VLAN-encapsulated packets and could leave the inner header improperly prepared. Switching to VLAN-aware preparation in the IPv6 tunnel receive path matches the described vulnerability fix.

candidates.rationale: This statement performs inner IP header validation/preparation using pskb_inet_may_pull(), which is the non-VLAN-aware helper identified in the root cause. Using this helper left VLAN-encapsulated sk_buffs improperly prepared, leading later ECN decapsulation to read uninitialized inner-header data.

vuln_statements.explanation: This line uses the non-VLAN-aware inner-header preparation helper in the IPv6 tunnel receive path. For VLAN-encapsulated sk_buffs, it could leave the inner IP header improperly prepared, so subsequent ECN decapsulation could read uninitialized inner-header data.

bic_trace_step.reason: The diff directly shows the vulnerable area in __ip6_tnl_rcv() and the added remediation, so the function body is sufficient. The root cause was that the function reset to the inner network header and then later used inner IP state without ensuring the inner header had been pulled/prepared for cases such as VLAN-encapsulated skb. In this commit, the fix is present: after `skb_reset_network_header(skb);` the code now calls `if (!pskb_inet_may_pull(skb)) { ... goto drop; }`, which is exactly the added validation/pull of the inner IP header. It also preserves the outer header location with `nh = skb_network_header(skb) - skb->head;` and reinitializes `ipv6h` afterward with `ipv6h = (struct ipv6hdr *)(skb->head + nh);`, matching the commit message that `skb->head` may change after the pull. Because this function version already includes the `pskb_inet_may_pull()` handling and the post-pull `ipv6h` reinitialization, the vulnerable construct is not present here, and the fix is present.
